label: early/delimiter steps after a prefix rich in i/a/g/o/j
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps). Fires at original-phase steps t>=2 and at the <DEL> step (39% of mass, but only 4.7% of DEL steps fire) when the inputs seen so far are dominated by the tokens i, a, g (strongest), o, j: at least 2 such tokens and they make up at least half the prefix. Rates rise with prev2_tok/prev_tok/first_tok in {i,a,g,o,j} (prev2_tok=i lift 6.8x). Strongest activations are on <DEL> of short sequences (L=3-4) consisting almost entirely of i/a/g/o (e.g. a i a <DEL>). Almost never fires at t=0-1 and rarely in the copy phase beyond the first output or two; weaker on long sequences. Precision is low (~0.2): many prefixes rich in these tokens do not fire, so the exact rule is not captured. Magnitude claims beyond top examples on short i/a/g prefixes at <DEL> were not checked.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=1 & in_tok=b (+6.35), t=1 & prev_tok=i (+4.69), orig2=a (+2.50), orig2=i (+2.32), orig1=a (+2.14), orig2=g (+2.11). Lower it: prev2_tok=- (-7.18), in_tok=a (-3.91), in_tok=g (-3.55), out_tok=b (-3.45).
